picks.style: greek moralist air, lyre, sparse frame drum, dry male voice, moderate, wry, clipped
picks.why: Two finished epigrams on silence — the benefits that attend silent lips, and miseries that spring not from unlocked houses but unbridled tongues.

picks.style: greek recitative, single kithara, spoken-sung baritone, unhurried, ironic
picks.why: Nature gave us two ears and one tongue, then the Euripidean quatrain about pouring wisdom into a skull that will hold nothing.

picks.style: greek tragic solo, lyre, low drone, aged male voice, very slow, luminous, valedictory
picks.why: Oedipus leading his own funeral procession — light of day, no light to me — the most famous exit in Greek tragedy.

picks.style: ancient chorus with narrator, aulos, frame drum, layered voices, hushed then swelling, uncanny
picks.why: The god calling out of nowhere — Oedipus, Oedipus, why do you delay our going — with everyone's hair rising from terror.

picks.style: pastoral prologue, lyre, soft flute, two voices, gentle, wandering, unhurried
picks.why: The blind old man asking where they have come, and Antigone answering with laurel, olive, vine and a crowd of nightingales.

picks.style: roman elegy, lyre and soft flute, wry male voice, easy lilt, playful, light
picks.why: Cupid stealing a foot from every second line — the joke that opens Latin love elegy, told entirely in itself.

picks.style: sensual roman air, kithara, low drum, warm male voice, slow, hushed, languid
picks.why: Corinna in the shuttered afternoon, hair loose, gown loose — the most famous elegy in the book and complete in itself.

picks.style: aubade, plucked lyre, soft strings, pleading male vocal, unhurried, dawn-lit
picks.why: The lover cursing the dawn, with the moon keeping her Endymion drowned in dewy sleep.

picks.style: english romantic art song, piano and cello, dark baritone, slow, solemn, inward
picks.why: Clean English throughout: the immortal mind as its own origin of ill and end, its own place and time.

picks.style: renaissance lament, lute and viol, tenor, plaintive, very slow, bare
picks.why: The Catullus brother-elegy in full — with thee my soul is all and whole enshrined — ending on a vow of love beyond death.

picks.style: balinese sacred chant, metallophone and small gong, drone, low male voice, slow, ritual, hypnotic
picks.why: The six limbs of yoga in couplets, ending on the gall-bladder dark in the heart's root and the Lord of the World at the end of the deepest dark.

picks.style: gamelan-backed recitation, soft gongs, bamboo flute, single voice, measured, meditative
picks.why: A stone for the people of the world, the Self for sages — then Maheśvara the size of a thumb, shining like crystal in the temple of the body.

picks.style: temple chant, drone and hand bell, layered male voices, slow, cyclical, incantatory
picks.why: The cosmogony as a chain — from the Unmanifest nāda, from nāda bindu, from bindu the moon, from the moon the universe, again and again.

picks.style: nordic war chant, bowed lyre, heavy frame drum, low male chorus, stark, driving, hard refrain
picks.why: Pharamond! Pharamond! we have fought with the sword — a real refrain, crows swimming in blood, and we will smile when we must die.

picks.style: medieval lament, solo female voice, bare vielle drone, no percussion, very slow, desolate
picks.why: The exiled woman asking the wind and the clouds for news, and swearing she would swim to them if the ship split.

picks.style: delphic hymn, lyre and aulos, clear male voice, bright, measured, serene
picks.why: A short chain of poets on what music suits which god — Apollo joys in pleasant tones, Pluto in griefs and moans.

picks.style: spare philosophical chant, single lyre, hushed male voice, very slow, questioning, echoing
picks.why: Two lines that carry the whole thought: who knows if to live is to be dead, and to be dead, to live.
